# cmux-fleet — Ideal State Artifact

Implements `Docs/SRD.md` (SRD-PIFLEET-001 v2.3). The SRD is the *design*; this ISA is the
*done condition*. Where they disagree, the ISA's criteria are what gets tested and the SRD
gets an erratum entry in `## Changelog`.

## Problem

Claude can drive one coding agent at a time, in its own context, at its own pace. Work that
decomposes into six independent investigations — six services to diagnose, six modules to
port, one fix plus five verifications — serializes anyway, because there is no way to hand a
task to a *separate* agent and get a trustworthy artifact back.

cmux can show N panes of N agents. That solves the *display*, not the *handoff*. Reading a
pane's rendered text back is lossy, racy, and unparseable: ANSI escapes, reflow on resize,
scrollback eviction, no completion signal. An orchestrator built on screen-scraping cannot
tell "the agent finished and succeeded" from "the agent printed the word success". And an
unsandboxed agent with a bash tool, pointed at a real repo with real cloud credentials, can
rewind a worktree or delete a deployment — that already happened once on this machine.

There is no tool that lets Claude configure a fleet, dispatch typed tasks to it, know
authoritatively when each task settled, and harvest each agent's work as structured
artifacts — with the blast radius bounded.

## Vision

Claude writes six task envelopes, runs one command, and walks away. Six containers wake up,
each with exactly the skills its role needs and no credential it does not need. cmux shows
six live panes — because a human wants to *watch* — but nothing about the run depends on
those panes existing. When the tasks settle, `pifleet artifacts --all --json` returns six
structured results whose claims have been checked against the actual git diffs, and a worker
that says it succeeded while changing nothing is reported as failed. The euphoric surprise is
that closing a pane, or never opening one, changes nothing at all.

## Out of Scope

Not in v1: a hosted/multi-user service; any non-Pi agent backend; Windows; running workers on
a remote host (all containers are local to the Docker host that also runs oMLX); a web UI;
automatic PR creation or merging by workers; cloud-hosted inference of any kind; cost
accounting in currency (local models are unpriced — `tokens_ceiling` is the only ceiling);
and autonomous task decomposition (Claude writes the envelopes; pifleet dispatches them).

The `tui` pane mode (Phase 6) is explicitly a *degraded* mode that voids ten requirements;
it is a convenience for attended debugging, not the supported path.

## Principles

- **The pane is a view, not a channel.** Every control-plane fact comes from the Pi RPC
  stream, the session transcript, or the outbox — never from rendered pane text. Presentation
  can be deleted without loss.
- **Ground truth is the installed binary.** Interfaces are verified by executing the pinned
  version, not by reading a documentation site. v1.1 of the SRD invented three protocol
  messages this way and would have hung on every task.
- **Self-report is a claim, not a fact.** A worker's own verdict is adjudicated against
  independent evidence (git diff, acceptance commands, transcript) before it is believed.
- **Least authority per role.** A role gets the credentials, tools, and skills its job needs
  and nothing else; the default is deny.
- **Failure must be loud and fast.** A wedged agent, a silent no-tool-call loop, or a blown
  budget terminates with a named diagnosis rather than hanging until a human notices.

## Constraints

- Bun + TypeScript. `bun test` is the test runner. No npm/yarn/pnpm (corporate proxy).
- Pi is pinned to **0.79.6**; cmux to **0.64.20**. Version drift fails `doctor`.
- Every worker runs inside a Docker container: read-only root, uid 10001, tini as PID 1.
- The LLM is **always** local oMLX on the Docker host (`host.docker.internal:8000`). No
  cloud inference, ever. No provider API key enters a container except `OMLX_API_KEY`.
- Google credentials enter containers as a ~1h **access token** only. A refresh token must
  never be present, and `~/.config/gcloud` is never mounted.
- Mutating `gcloud`/`kubectl`/`helm` verbs pass through the `verbgate` PATH shim and require
  task-scoped authorization.
- No AI attribution in any commit message, PR description, or code comment.
- The `headless` backend must run the entire acceptance suite with cmux not installed.

## Goal

`pifleet` is a Bun CLI that brings up a configurable fleet of containerized Pi 0.79.6 workers
— optionally surfaced as cmux panes — accepts typed task envelopes, detects completion
authoritatively via `agent_end{willRetry:false}` plus a correlated `get_state` fence, and
returns adjudicated structured artifacts, with all 160 criteria below passing and the full
suite green on `headless` against a test double.

## Criteria

**Checkbox meanings.** A criterion earns `[x]` only when something REPRODUCIBLE re-checks
it — a test that runs in CI and covers what the criterion literally says. `[~]` means
partially proved: the note states exactly which half is machine-checked and which half rests
on a hand-run on a developer host, and `[~]` does NOT count toward `progress:`. `[ ]` is
open. A live probe that self-skips in CI when a real dependency is unavailable is CORRECT
and should stay — but a criterion resting only on such a probe is `[~]`, not `[x]`. This
distinction was introduced 2026-08-19 after a sibling branch found a criterion marked `[x]`
on evidence that turned out to be falsified; the ISA is a system of record, so it has to
earn that.

**`[-]` means RETIRED (introduced 2026-08-30 by ISC-368).** The criterion's PREMISE was
superseded, so the sentence describes an intention this system no longer has. A retired
criterion is excluded from `progress:` on BOTH sides — it leaves the numerator and the
denominator — and the frontmatter's `retired:` line reports how many left, so the figure is
`<checked>/<live>` with the remainder stated rather than absorbed. **Retiring is not
closing:** no credit is earned, and a criterion is never retired to avoid grading it.
**Retiring is not deleting:** the entry, its text and its id all stay, and so do the
registered claims in `test/support/isa-claims.ts` that carried it — a guard over shipped
code outlives the document sentence it was filed under. **Retiring is not available to a
criterion that is merely hard, slow or inconvenient to evidence:** the entry must name the
CLOSED criterion that superseded its premise, and that criterion must name it back.
`test/unit/isa-retired.test.ts` enforces every clause of that, and `[~]` remains the honest
grade for anything that is simply not yet proved.

Machine-checked at two altitudes, both of which EXECUTE in CI. `test/unit/container-env.test.ts` (4 probes, no daemon, runs in the fast `test` job on every push via `bun test test/unit`) enumerates EVERY `docker run` argv builder in `src/` — `buildDockerArgv`, `relayRunArgv`, `containerProbeArgv` — and requires that no `-e`/`--env` before the image names a cloud credential. It enforces TWO rules, and the second is the sharp one: `-e NAME=value` is auditable by reading it, but the BARE `-e NAME` form silently passes the HOST's value through into the container and appears in `docker inspect` while the argv a reviewer reads contains nothing secret-looking. The bare form is refused outright rather than inspected. Names are matched both against `adc.ts`'s own `CREDENTIAL_ENV_VARS` (imported, not retyped) and against a structural secret shape, so an unenumerated `FOOCLOUD_API_KEY` is caught too; `*_FILE` is excluded deliberately, because `CLOUDSDK_AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE` is the POINTER whose whole purpose is to keep the token out of the environment. `test/integration/container-env.test.ts` is the criterion's literal instrument — it `docker inspect`s `.Config.Env` on a real container and is Docker-gated, so it is NEWLY WIRED into the `container` job (`TOTAL_EXPECTED` 79 -> 81, re-derived by the documented hand method: gate unset gives `2 pass, 79 skip, Ran 81 tests across 7 files`). It needs only a daemon and the worker image — no host Google credential, no inference server — so it contributes 2 pass / 0 skip there and is pinned in no skip list. It matters that this altitude exists: the image's baked `ENV` is inside `.Config.Env`, so a Dockerfile that started baking a key would be invisible to every argv assertion in the repo. THREE MUTATIONS, all confirmed RED and reverted. (C) `argv.push("-e", "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=…")` in `buildDockerArgv` -> unit half red: `Expected: not "worker eng-1: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"`. (D) the bare form `argv.push("-e", "FOOCLOUD_API_KEY")` -> red on a name in NO enumerated list: `Expected: "worker eng-1 sets FOOCLOUD_API_KEY (secret-shaped: false)" / Received: "… (secret-shaped: true)"`, and the source-level sweep for the bare form went red simultaneously. (E) the same literal key against the live daemon -> integration half red: `Expected: "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY (secret-shaped: false)" / Received: "… (secret-shaped: true)"`, i.e. the key really did reach the container and `docker inspect` really did report it. STATED LIMITATION, because it bounds what the live half means: `up` launches no worker container today — nothing in `src/` execs `buildDockerArgv`'s output (ISC-248) — so the integration probe EXECUTES production's own rendered argv rather than observing a container a real run left behind, and it writes the `--env-file` empty because production deliberately writes it not at all (`run/materialize.ts` explains why). Empty is the honest stand-in: it adds nothing, so what is inspected is exactly the image's baked `ENV` plus the argv's `-e` set, which is the surface the criterion names.
- [x] ISC-32: `up` refuses to start when a role's image is missing. **NOT IMPLEMENTED — stays open, and the reason it looked otherwise has been removed.** No test named it (`grep -rn 'ISC-32\b' test/` returns nothing; the only hits anywhere in the tree are the two docstring back-references this grading itself added, in `src/container/image.ts` and `src/cli/commands/image.ts`, which are pointers to this entry and not coverage) and no code implements it. Measured, not inferred: `grep -in image src/cli/commands/up.ts` returns ZERO lines — `up.ts` does not contain the string at all; `verifyImage` has exactly one caller in the tree (`cli/commands/image.ts`, the `image verify` subcommand); and NONE of the three `docker image inspect` calls in `src/` is on `up`'s path — `doctor.ts`'s `imageStatus` REPORTS and `up.ts` does not import it, and the other two are `container/image.ts`'s `listImages` and `verifyImage`, reached only from the operator-driven `image list` / `image gc` / `image verify` subcommands. `config/render.ts` calls `imageTag` solely to place the tag into the `docker run` argv. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS with a missing image, which is the opposite of a refusal: `up` creates the run directory, clones a checkout per worker, registers a remote per worker in the OPERATOR's repository, materializes every input, launches every supervisor, and only then meets the idle gate at the end of the command — where the dead child surfaces as `worker <id> died during startup` with `EXIT.WORKER_DIED` (or `EXIT.TIMEOUT`), leaving the whole run's state on disk. "Refuses to start" and "starts everything, then reports a corpse" are different exit codes, different diagnoses, and different amounts of cleanup. WHY THIS READ AS CLOSED: three docstrings in `src/` asserted the control. `container/image.ts`'s header carried ISC-189's sentence VERBATIM ("`up` refuses to run against an image that is absent or fails `verify`"), its `ImageInputs` doc said "`up`, which only refuses an image that is ABSENT", and `cli/commands/image.ts` said "`verify` failing is load-bearing: `up` refuses to start on it". All three are now corrected in place to state what the code does and to point back here — a comment is not a control, and this is the same defect class the module has been patched for twice already. Beyond the exit code the test pins THREE independent ordering witnesses, because "refuses" is a claim about ORDER and an exit code alone cannot carry it: the docker call log holds `image inspect` and ZERO `network `/`run ` lines; `git -C repo remote` is empty, so no per-worker remote reached the operator's repository; and the run dir has an empty `workersDir` and an empty ledger. A second test uses worker `rev-1` on role `reviewer`, so a gate that echoes the worker id and calls it the role cannot pass. Daemon-free — the docker PATH shim answers `image inspect` — so it runs in the fast `test` job.

- [x] ISC-270: Every `COPY` source in `docker/Dockerfile` appears in `BUILD_CONTEXT_ASSETS`. **FILED OPEN 2026-08-19, and filed rather than fixed deliberately — the array is CORRECT today, so there is nothing to repair; what is missing is the thing that keeps it correct.** Measured now, so a future grader inherits the baseline instead of re-deriving it: `BUILD_CONTEXT_ASSETS` is the hand-maintained three-element array `["Dockerfile", "verbgate", "entrypoint.sh"]` (`src/container/image.ts`), and the only `COPY` sources in `docker/Dockerfile` are `docker/verbgate` (five times, lines 78-82) and `docker/entrypoint.sh` (line 164) — so the array covers the build context exactly, plus the Dockerfile itself. **THE FAIL-OPEN.** `configHash` hashes the content of every file in that array and nothing else, and the array is maintained BY HAND. Add a file the Dockerfile `COPY`s without adding it to the array and the hash does not move, the tag does not move, and a stale image is silently reused — with nothing anywhere reporting it. The failure is silent in both directions that matter: the build succeeds, and the run succeeds against the wrong bytes. **WHY IT IS ITS OWN CRITERION.** This is the flank of ISC-160 ("a stale image is not silently reused after the Dockerfile changed"), which is `[x]` and genuinely proved — but proved for edits to files ALREADY in the array. ISC-160 does not, and cannot, observe a file that was never enrolled. Until now the gap lived only as a subordinate clause inside `ISC-189`'s note and as prose in the header of `container/image.ts` — i.e. inside the very module it describes, which is the arrangement that let three docstrings in this same module assert controls the code did not have. A gap named in prose by the thing it afflicts is not tracked; it is annotated. **TO CLOSE — and note how cheap it is.** One unit test: parse `docker/Dockerfile`, extract every `COPY` source under `docker/`, assert the set is a subset of `BUILD_CONTEXT_ASSETS`. No daemon, no image build, no Docker-gated job — it reads two files off disk, so it runs in the fast `test` job on every PR. **It does NOT depend on the `up` image gate that ISC-32 and ISC-189 are waiting on**, and must not be bundled into that work: those two need a new control on the launch path, this needs a subset assertion over two files that already exist. Blocking a five-minute test on a design decision about `up` is how this gap stayed prose for as long as it did. *(CLOSED 2026-08-20, Phase B. `test/unit/dockerfile-build-assets.test.ts` + `test/support/dockerfile-copy.ts` parse `docker/Dockerfile` and set-compare against `BUILD_CONTEXT_ASSETS`. The reader folds line continuations, strips `#` comments, handles shell and JSON-array operand forms, drops the destination, and excludes the three legitimately unhashable source kinds (`--from=<stage>`, `ADD https://`, heredocs). It reads `ADD` ALONGSIDE `COPY`, deliberately: this criterion is worded over `COPY` because that is the instruction in use today, but the failure it describes is 'a context file reaches the image without reaching the hash', and `ADD <local path>` does exactly that — reading only `COPY` would leave a one-keyword bypass. 19 tests, including an anti-vacuity clause asserting the parse found >=6 sources resolving to exactly {verbgate, entrypoint.sh}. MUTATION-PROVED: adding `COPY docker/somefile /x` fails the named test with a message naming the file and the consequence ('edit that file and the tag does not move, and a stale image is reused silently'); Dockerfile restored to 177 lines, 19/19.)*

### Group D — Google credentials

- [x] ISC-41: With `cloud_access: true` and `adc_mode: token`, `gcloud auth print-access-token` succeeds inside the container. **PARTIAL — the positive case is proved on a developer host only.** It had been marked `[x]` with NO evidence and was in fact FALSE as shipped: `grep -rn 'ISC-41\b' test/` returned only comment references, no test named it, and no test in `test/integration/adc.test.ts` invoked `gcloud` at all — while ISC-255's measured `[Errno 30]` crash meant every gcloud call in a real worker failed even with a valid credential. MACHINE-CHECKED, every CI run: `test/unit/render.test.ts` proves `buildDockerArgv` emits the writable gcloud-config tmpfs for every role (mutation-proved), and `adc.test.ts`'s "the gcloud config dir is writable by the worker uid" probe proves the container that flag produces is actually writable by uid 10001 on a tmpfs — the precondition whose absence made this criterion false. **[RE-GRADED `[~]` -> `[x]` 2026-08-27 — the sentence that follows was TRUE when written and is now FALSE, and the code did not change.]** This read *"LOCAL ONLY, not re-checked anywhere automated"* of the one probe the criterion turns on. PR #82 gave the `container` job a keyless federated credential, and `hostAdcFile()` honours `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` — so `HOST_ADC_PRESENT` became true through the PRODUCTION lookup rule rather than a test-only branch, and the probe un-skipped without a line of it changing. VERIFIED BY READING CI, not by inferring it from the config: run 33032039999, `container` job — `(pass) ... with cloud_access and a token, gcloud auth print-access-token succeeds (ISC-41) [2215.05ms]`. The guard that keeps it honest is `EXPECTED_HOST_ADC_MINT_SKIPS: ""` — empty, so a probe that SKIPPED in that job would fail the build rather than pass quietly. The evidence: real `gcloud auth print-access-token` inside the production container shape exits 0, returns the injected token (compared by sha256 so a failure never prints a bearer token), and leaves stderr EMPTY. That is `adc.test.ts`'s "with cloud_access and a token, gcloud auth print-access-token succeeds (ISC-41)", which mints a genuine ~1h token through the production `gcloudMinter` from the host's own ADC and asserts exit 0, stdout equal to the minted token (compared by sha256 digest so a failure never prints a live bearer token), and stderr EMPTY — empty stderr being load-bearing, since the root-owned-tmpfs near-miss also exits 0 while warning on every call. It is `test.skipIf(!HOST_ADC_PRESENT)` and skips on every CI runner, because no runner has an operator's Google login and no synthetic file can stand in for one. Run against `/usr/local/libexec/gcloud.real`, deliberately bypassing the PATH `verbgate` wrapper — see ISC-46 for why, and for the recorded consequence that the PATH form never exits 0 in a real worker. Verified locally 2026-08-19: 18/18 in `adc.test.ts` with a real host ADC present.

- [x] ISC-44: The host `~/.config/gcloud` directory is not in any container's `docker inspect` mount list. Fully machine-checked in CI, at two altitudes. `test/unit/render.test.ts` (no daemon, runs everywhere) asserts the ARGV `renderWorker`/`buildDockerArgv` would launch never names `hostGcloudConfigDir()`, for a `cloud_access: false` role and a `cloud_access: true, adc_mode: file` role alike. `test/integration/adc.test.ts` (Docker-gated only — no host credential needed, so it runs in the container job) `docker inspect`s real containers in the role shapes §5.8 can produce and asserts no `.Mounts[].Source` is, is under, or CONTAINS the host directory, with the one documented exception of the single ADC file `file` mode may mount. THREE CORRECTIONS this round. (1) The ANCESTOR direction was entirely missing: both altitudes asked only whether a source was the store or sat UNDER it, so mounting `$HOME` or `$HOME/.config` handed over the whole multi-account auth store and passed every assertion — reachable through supported config, since `run.repo` is operator-settable and is mounted at `/workspace`. Worse, the unit check routed through `runStateHostPaths`, which DROPS every `/workspace` mount, so it was structurally blind to the one mount that could do this. Both now use `classifyHostGcloudExposure`, production's own three-relation predicate, and `assertNoHostGcloudMount` runs it inside `buildDockerArgv` itself, so the criterion is ENFORCED at launch rather than merely asserted about — the constants previously had zero importers in `src/` and closed nothing. A dedicated test drives `run.repo: ~` and `run.repo: ~/.config` through `renderWorker` and requires a `HostGcloudMountError`; mutation-proved by deleting the guard. (2) Mount sources are `realpath`-normalised on both sides in the integration check — a lexical compare passes a symlinked source (`/tmp -> /private/tmp` on macOS is the everyday case) or an APFS case variant. (3) The `file`-mode case is now marked FORWARD-LOOKING rather than production-verified, and honestly so: nothing in `src/` mounts an ADC file — `buildDockerArgv` emits no `/creds` mount and `fileModeMaterials`/`fileModeStartupEnv`/`ADC_FILE_PATH` have no production caller — so that test hand-writes the `-v` itself and inspects a shape it authored. It pins the contract `file` mode must satisfy when wired; it is not evidence about a launch `up` can perform today. It is also now CI-runnable via `PIFLEET_TEST_ADC_FILE` (it needs a FILE, not a valid credential), where before it silently ran in no job at all. **[AMENDED 2026-08-20 — the criterion still holds and STAYS `[x]`; what changes is the history, because the evidence above was incomplete until this branch and a future grader needs to know how.]** The three corrections recorded above are all real and all still stand. None of them examined whether the PREDICATE could see, and on two counts it could not — the same two counts, arrived at INDEPENDENTLY, as the run-dir guard this one is deliberately shaped like. (1) **The filesystem root.** `store.startsWith(`${s}/`)` builds `"//"` when the source is `/`, and no path starts with `"//"`, so **`-v /:/host` handed over the entire host gcloud auth store** — every account the operator has ever logged in — and `classifyHostGcloudExposure` returned `null`. The ancestor direction that correction (1) above was written to add was therefore still open at its widest point: `$HOME` was caught, `$HOME/.config` was caught, and `/` was not. (2) **Three of four Docker bind-mount spellings.** `assertNoHostGcloudMount` scanned for a two-element `-v`/`--volume` only, so `--volume=<src>:<dst>`, `-v<src>:<dst>` and `--mount type=bind,source=…` — all valid docker, all mounting the store — walked past it. Latent, since `render.ts` emits one spelling, and latent is the argument for closing it: this guard's own stated justification is that the offending path arrives from operator config rather than from an auditable literal, so depending on upstream to keep spelling the FLAG one way re-imports the assumption the guard was built to remove. **BOTH GUARDS HAD BOTH BUGS, SEPARATELY, AND THAT IS THE POINT.** Each carried its own copy of the boundary comparison, each copy was wrong the same way, and neither could catch the other because they shared no line. They now share one definition — `isPathUnder` / `pathsEqual`, exported from `run/paths.ts` — and one argv reader, `bindMountSources` (`container/docker-argv.ts`). Two copies of a boundary cannot check each other; one definition can at least be pinned once. **MUTATIONS, both RED and reverted, against a 62 pass / 0 fail baseline** (`bun test test/unit/render.test.ts test/unit/container-env.test.ts`). Root: restoring the bare `${a}/` prefix reddens `the filesystem root is refused by the gcloud guard too (ISC-44)` with `Expected: "/ -> contains-the-store" / Received: "/ -> null"`. Spellings: narrowing the shared parser to the two-element form reddens `every docker bind-mount spelling reaches the gcloud guard (ISC-44)` with `Expected: "glued --volume= -> HostGcloudMountError" / Received: "glued --volume= -> ALLOWED"`. **That second test is deliberately its own case rather than left to the shared parser's ISC-127 test**, and the reason generalises: when two criteria depend on one piece of shared code, the criterion that depends on a behaviour must be the one that goes red when the behaviour is removed — otherwise someone narrowing the parser sees a single red test named for the RUN DIRECTORY and reasonably concludes the auth store is unaffected. **Also fixed here:** `HostGcloudMountError` carried no `exitCode`, so a refused mount surfaced as `pifleet: internal error:` rather than as the config refusal it is; it is now `EXIT.USAGE`, graded identically to `RunDirMountError` because the two are built to be indistinguishable from the outside. **NOT re-graded to `[ ]` and back.** A checkbox records whether the criterion holds with reproducible evidence; it does, and churning the mark inside one branch would inform nobody. The gap was in the evidence, so the evidence is what this note repairs. See ISC-127's close-out for the full account, including the independent-backstop failure that made this class visible: a hand-written cross-check written specifically NOT to share production's predicate reproduced that predicate's root bug exactly, and ran 1 pass / 0 fail against a mount table containing `-v /:/host`.
- [x] ISC-45: A role with `cloud_access: false` has no Google credential. Machine-checked in CI at two altitudes; no host credential needed for either. `test/integration/adc.test.ts` (Docker-gated) starts a container in the exact env `planCredential` returns for such a role — empty: no pointer, no token file, no `/creds` content — and probes both a fresh `env` and `/proc/1/environ` (the two can differ) for all four delivery vars, with a same-image contrast test on an injected `token`-mode container showing every one of those things present, so the absence is a property of the ROLE, not of the image. `test/unit/render.test.ts` adds the cheap always-runs counterpart the criterion previously lacked: for a `cloud_access: false` worker, neither the rendered argv nor the rendered `--env-file` names any of `CREDENTIAL_ENV_VARS` — the env-file specifically, because §5.6 delivers a worker's environment that way and the integration rig's `-e` flags exercise a path production does not use. THE VECTOR SET WAS OVERSOLD as "four env vars" and is corrected: `$CLOUDSDK_CONFIG` was the vector this suite had blinded itself to (ISC-255) and is now swept and asserted empty; `/home/pi/.kube/config` — the ONLY credential-bearing mount `buildDockerArgv` actually emits today, gated on `cloud.kubeconfig !== null && w.cloudAccess`, and a kubeconfig with a `gcp` auth-provider or an embedded token IS a Google credential — now has its own probe asserting the mount point is empty for such a role; and the GCE metadata fallback at 169.254.169.254 is closed by `--network none`, which `startContainer` now applies by default.
- [x] ISC-46: In a `cloud_access: false` role, `gcloud auth print-access-token` fails. The criterion as literally worded — FAILS without a credential — is machine-checked in CI: both probes are Docker-gated only and need no host credential. The first runs `/usr/local/libexec/gcloud.real` (the real binary, bypassing the PATH `verbgate` wrapper deliberately: verbgate classifies this verb as MUTATING regardless of credential state per ISC-210, a §5.10 concern orthogonal to this one, so testing through it would measure the gate rather than the credential) and requires gcloud's own credential-absence message, not merely a nonzero exit — so the test cannot be satisfied by gcloud being missing (127) or gated (77). That message is now matched by REGEX on the invariant fragments rather than pinned verbatim: it is google-cloud-cli's English, the image installs the SDK unpinned, and CI rebuilds the image every run, so an exact string was a false red waiting on an upstream copy edit. The second probe is new and covers the criterion's LITERAL command through PATH, where an agent actually types it: `gcloud auth print-access-token` exits 77 with verbgate's refusal. THE CONSEQUENCE IS RECORDED because it surprises anyone reading the criterion straight: in a real worker this command never exits 0, credential or no credential, so ISC-46 holds for a STRONGER reason than it claims. **Local only, not re-checked in CI:** the positive control — the same command in the same container flipping exit 1 to exit 0 once a REAL minted token is injected, with stdout equal to the token by sha256 digest. That is `test.skipIf(!HOST_ADC_PRESENT)` and skips on every runner. It is the strongest evidence in the block and it rests on a developer host; the criterion is nonetheless `[x]` because what it literally asserts (failure in the absence of a credential) is fully covered by the two CI-runnable probes.
- [x] ISC-47: After `token_refresh` elapses, a `gcloud` call inside a long-running container still succeeds. **PARTIAL — proved on a developer host only, and only the in-container half.** Like ISC-41 this had been marked `[x]` with NO evidence (`grep -rn 'ISC-47\b' test/` found only comments) and was equally falsified by ISC-255. The evidence is `adc.test.ts`'s "a gcloud call still succeeds after a refresh re-injection (ISC-47)": one long-running container, a real minted token injected, gcloud verified to return exactly that token, then a SECOND genuinely separate mint injected through the same production `injectToken` the refresh loop drives, and gcloud verified to return the NEW value — so the assertion is that the refresh took effect, not that a cached credential kept working. It is `test.skipIf(!HOST_ADC_PRESENT)` and SKIPS IN CI; nothing automated re-checks it. Two further gaps, stated plainly rather than smoothed over: (1) the re-injection stands in for the elapsed interval deliberately — sleeping out a real `token_refresh` costs minutes of wall clock and would measure the supervisor's timer, which is `supervisor.test.ts`'s monotonic-clock territory (ISC-155); (2) nothing in `src/cli/**` mints or injects at all yet (ISC-248; see ISC-48 on `gcloudMinter` having no caller), so this proves a mechanism, not that a live `up` run ever refreshes anything. **[RE-GRADED `[~]` -> `[x]` 2026-08-27. Both stated gaps are closed, and BOTH were closed by other work rather than by anything done to this criterion.]** **Gap (2) — *"nothing in `src/cli/**` mints or injects at all yet (ISC-248) … so this proves a mechanism, not that a live `up` run ever refreshes anything"* — is FALSE as of `ed67bf2`.** The supervisor now constructs a `TokenRefresher` on its own lifecycle and drives `run(signal)`: a live run mints and injects, and re-injects on the configured interval. **Gap (1) — the re-injection standing in for an ELAPSED interval — is closed by ISC-248's probe**, which is not a stand-in: `token_refresh` is compressed to 2s in CONFIG, the interval genuinely elapses, and generation 1 appears in `credentials.jsonl` because the loop fired. **And the CI-skip sentence above is stale on the same evidence as ISC-41**: run 33032039999, `container` job — `(pass) ... a gcloud call still succeeds after a refresh re-injection (ISC-47) [3465.08ms]`. **What composes to the criterion, stated so the composition is not overread.** ISC-47 asks that a `gcloud` call still succeed after `token_refresh` elapses. The elapse is proved by ISC-248's probe (real supervisor, real container, real credential, interval elapsed); the gcloud-still-works half is proved by this file's probe against a second genuinely-separate mint through the same production `injectToken` the loop drives. Both run in CI on every run of the `container` job. **A single probe doing both would be stronger and is recorded as the remaining improvement, not as a gap in the claim**: ISC-248's probe uses `alpine`, which has no gcloud, so proving both limbs in one test means re-running it against the worker image. **Still out of scope, unchanged:** that the supervisor's timer fires at the REAL 45-minute interval is `supervisor.test.ts`'s monotonic-clock territory (ISC-155); nothing here waits out 45 minutes of wall clock to measure a `setTimeout`.
- [x] ISC-48: With `impersonate_service_account` set, the token's identity is the SA, not the launching user's account. **PARTIAL — the criterion names a TOKEN, and no token is ever minted.** MACHINE-CHECKED, every CI run (`test/integration/up-wiring.test.ts`, real CLI, real `adc.ts`, PATH-shimmed `gcloud`/`docker`, no Docker daemon or host credential required): every worker's grant line names the configured SA and never the shimmed operator account nor the `"(adc user)"` placeholder — substitution, not coexistence — and (the actual security property) the operator's own account is never even asked for, the `gcloud` shim's call log being empty for a run where every `cloud_access` worker impersonates, against a control run that logs exactly one `config get-value account`. That empty log is now itself verified: before `up` runs, the test drives one throwaway `gcloud` call through THAT RIG's own PATH and asserts it landed in THAT RIG's log, then truncates — previously the only control was a DIFFERENT rig, so a shim that failed to install in the impersonating rig produced an empty log and a green test, which is the exact hazard the control claimed to close. Mutation-proved: widening `up.ts`'s resolve-identity guard to fire regardless of impersonation leaves every grant line byte-identical and only the call-count assertion goes red. **NOT PROVED, and the blocker is structural rather than environmental — the previous close-out named the wrong one.** It said no such SA was available on this host; the larger truth is that `gcloudMinter` has NO CALLER ANYWHERE IN `src/cli/**` (`up.ts` plans and prints, then stops — ISC-248), so no `up` path mints in any configuration and there is no token whose identity could be checked. Even when it is wired, note that impersonation is DELEGATED: at real mint time the operator's ADC IS used to obtain the SA token, so "the launching user's account is never consulted" is true of PLANNING and cannot be true of the mint itself. Separately, no real granted SA was available to test against — the SRD's example project is not reachable under this host's identity, and the only discoverable service accounts belong to a live production project, so impersonating one for this personal project's suite was deliberately avoided. **[RE-GRADED `[~]` -> `[x]` 2026-08-27. BOTH stated blockers are now false, and neither was removed by anything done to this criterion.]** **Blocker one — *"`gcloudMinter` has NO CALLER ANYWHERE IN `src/cli/**`"* — died with ISC-248.** The supervisor mints on its own lifecycle, so a token exists whose identity can be asked about. **Blocker two — *"no real granted SA was available to test against"* — was environmental and is resolved.** The old entry's refusal was correct on its facts: the only discoverable service accounts belonged to a live production project, and impersonating one for a personal project's suite was rightly declined. The target now used, `cmux-fleet-impersonated`, lives in the SAME personal project as the CI identity, exists for this purpose, and `cmux-fleet-ci` already held `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on it — verified by reading the SA's IAM policy back, not assumed. Nothing was created to close this. **The probe asks GOOGLE, not the argv**, and it took two attempts to ask correctly. `adc.test.ts`'s "with impersonate_service_account set, the token is the SA's, not the operator's (ISC-48)" mints through the production `gcloudMinter` with impersonation and sends the token to the standard introspection endpoint — in a POST BODY, since a bearer token in a query string lands in logs. **IT TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS TO ASK CORRECTLY, AND BOTH FAILURES WERE MINE RATHER THAN THE PRODUCT'S — recorded because the shape of the mistake is the reusable part.** The first asserted `email === <SA>` on the impersonated token and failed in CI with the literal string `(tokeninfo named no identity)`: a fallback that was a second defect in its own right, a diagnostic reporting only its own inability to answer. The second returned the claims whole — safe, because the response echoes claims and never the credential — but moved the SAME assumption onto the control, asserting that the un-impersonated mint reports an `email`. It does not, in CI, and that failure is the useful one. **WHICH CLAIM CARRIES THE IDENTITY DEPENDS ON THE CREDENTIAL, and both reachable shapes were introspected rather than assumed.** The operator's LOCAL ADC is a user credential: `email` + `sub` + `azp` (the gcloud client id) + `aud`, with `openid` and `userinfo.email` among its scopes. The operator's CI credential is federated and ALREADY A SERVICE ACCOUNT: it returns `azp=106755930525734032049` and NOTHING else — no `email`, no `sub`, scope `cloud-platform` ALONE. `gcloud iam service-accounts describe` confirms that number is `cmux-fleet-ci`'s `uniqueId`, so tokeninfo does name the principal there; it simply uses a different field. The rule underneath both measurements: an access token carries `email` only when its scopes include `openid`/`userinfo.email`, and a service-account token is minted with cloud-platform alone. **So every assertion is over the SET of identity-bearing claims — `email`, `sub`, `azp` — and none of them names a field.** `aud` is deliberately excluded: it names the token's AUDIENCE, not who is presenting it, so including it would let a shared audience read as a shared identity. **Three assertions, in this order:** a CONTROL — the un-impersonated mint names SOMEBODY, without which tokeninfo cannot see identity here and nothing below means anything; SUBSTITUTION — the impersonated token's claim set is DISJOINT from the control's, which is the criterion's literal "not the launching user's account" and which a silent fallback cannot dodge by surfacing the same principal under a different key; and POSITIVELY the SA — the service account's numeric `uniqueId`, resolved from the SA itself via `gcloud iam service-accounts describe` rather than hardcoded, appears among the token's claims. The positive half exists because disjointness ALONE would also be satisfied by a token belonging to some THIRD principal. Asserting that `mintArgv` carried `--impersonate-service-account` would prove we ASKED for impersonation, not that we got it, and the criterion is about which identity the issued token actually carries. **The contrast case is the load-bearing half:** the same minter WITHOUT impersonation must not come back as the SA. Without it, a tokeninfo response that named the SA unconditionally — or a target string that happened to equal the operator's own account — would read as success. **The delegation caveat from the previous entry STANDS and is not closed by this.** At real mint time the operator's ADC IS used to obtain the SA token, so "the launching user's account is never consulted" is true of PLANNING (`up-wiring.test.ts`'s empty shim log) and cannot be true of the mint itself. What this criterion claims, and all it claims, is that the ISSUED TOKEN's identity is the SA. **CI-only, stated rather than hidden:** the `tokenCreator` binding is granted to `cmux-fleet-ci` alone, so minting impersonated from a developer host returns `IAM_PERMISSION_DENIED` and the probe self-skips with a message naming what it needs. Granting the role to a HUMAN account to make it locally runnable was deliberately not done. **One IAM change WAS made and is recorded here rather than left to be discovered:** `cmux-fleet-ci` held no project-level roles at all and no permission to READ the SA it may impersonate, so `service-accounts describe` would have failed in CI. It was granted `roles/iam.serviceAccountViewer` on that one service account — read-only, scoped to a single resource, and the alternative was hardcoding the `uniqueId` into the test, which would compare a constant against itself the day the SA is recreated. **AND THE PROBE FOUND A HOLE IN THE CI CREDENTIAL SETUP, which is worth more than the criterion it was written for.** `service-accounts describe` failed in CI with `Failed to load credential file: [.../gha-creds-<id>.json]. File ... was not found` — a path the "Move the federated credential out of the workspace" step had itself relocated minutes earlier. That step re-points `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` and calls `gcloud auth login --force --cred-file`, and its own comment says it does so because "leaving it dangling would break any plain `gcloud` call the probes make". It did not: `google-github-actions/auth` also exports `CLOUDSDK_AUTH_CREDENTIAL_FILE_OVERRIDE`, an ENV OVERRIDE gcloud reads in preference to the account store, still naming the workspace path. So every plain `gcloud <api>` call in that job was broken, and it stayed invisible because nothing made one — the ADC mints follow `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` and were fine, and the step's own verification only exercised that half. Both stores are now re-pointed by COMPARISON with the source path (a variable naming something else is warned about, not overwritten), and the step now proves BOTH mints before the job proceeds rather than leaving one to fail twenty minutes later.
- [x] ISC-49: `up` prints the granted identity, project, and ADC mode for every `cloud_access` worker. Machine-checked in CI (`test/integration/up-wiring.test.ts` needs no Docker daemon and no host credential): a real `up` run over three workers (two `cloud_access: true` sharing one role, one `cloud_access: false`) with `cloud.adc_mode: file` and a distinctive `cloud.quota_project` asserts every line is keyed by worker id (not merely found), that both cloud workers' lines carry identity + the distinctive project + `"file mode"` (and explicitly not `"token mode"`, so a line ignoring `cloud.adc_mode` is caught), and that the non-cloud worker's line says `"no credential"` and carries none of the three. A companion test confirms the lines reach actual stdout, not only the ledger, when `--json` is absent. THE IDENTITY WAS COMING FROM THE WRONG CREDENTIAL STORE and is fixed. `resolveIdentity` read `gcloud config get-value account` — the `gcloud auth login` account — but `mintArgv` mints from ADC and `file` mode hands over `application_default_credentials.json`; these are separate stores written by separate commands and they routinely differ, so the printed line could name an identity the worker was never granted, in BOTH modes, and the suite asserted that line was correct. It now prefers the ADC file's own principal (`client_email` for service-account ADC, `account` for `authorized_user`) and falls back to the config account only when the file cannot name one — which is not hypothetical: measured on this host, `gcloud auth application-default login` wrote `"account": ""`, present and EMPTY, so the fallback is load-bearing rather than decorative. A fixture whose two stores DISAGREE on purpose pins it, since on a machine where they match (the common case, and the case here) no test could tell them apart; mutation-proved by reverting to config-first, which turns only that test red. `hostAdcFile()` also now honours `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, gcloud's own ADC override — deliberately NOT applied to `hostGcloudConfigDir()`, since letting an env var redirect a security boundary is how the boundary stops meaning anything. Also corrected: a `String(r.detail?.["plan"])` in the ledger helper yielded the literal string `"undefined"` on a missing field, which is truthy, non-empty, and contains none of the things the ISC-48/49 tests assert are absent — every `not.toContain` in this file was vacuous against a dropped field. The type is now asserted before coercion.

### Group E — Local model (oMLX)

- [x] ISC-50: A container completes a model call against `host.docker.internal:8000`. **[PARTIAL 2026-08-19 — DOWNGRADED from [x] by the PR #18 security review]** The MECHANISM is closed and unconditional: `test/integration/relay.test.ts`'s stub test proves a container attached to nothing but the deny-all internal bridge — no `--add-host`, no second network, no capabilities — completes a `GET http://host.docker.internal:<port>/v1/models` and receives the upstream's OWN body, carrying a nonce that cannot have been synthesized by Docker, on an EPHEMERAL port (which is what proves the port is read from `llm.base_url` rather than hardcoded). **Why this is no longer `[x]`:** the LIVE half — the same call against the real oMLX server, which is what ties the mechanism to the actual model server — self-skips when oMLX or `OMLX_API_KEY` is absent, and oMLX here binds `127.0.0.1:8000`, LOOPBACK ONLY. The live path therefore depends on Lima's host-gateway forwarding reaching macOS loopback: an environment property of this laptop, not a property of pifleet, and one that will not hold on a CI runner or on native Docker. Combined with ISC-257 (this suite runs in NO CI job at all), a criterion whose live evidence can only ever execute on one machine is `[~]`, not `[x]`. **Stated limit, unchanged:** what is asserted is a call to the model SERVER, not an INFERENCE — a real `POST /v1/chat/completions` was measured round-tripping through the relay by hand on 2026-08-19 (705 ms warm, correct answer from inside the bridge), but that measurement is deliberately not a test; see ISC-258. **[CLOSED 2026-08-25 by the `container-live` CI job — every one of the three reasons this was `[~]` is now answered, and by measurement rather than by argument.]** run 32797559555 job 97651850285, `container-live` on `ubuntu-latest`: `pass=9 fail=0 skip=0 todo=0 total=9 expected=9 rc=0`, empty pin list. **(a) The live half no longer self-skips:** it runs with `EXPECTED_CONTAINER_LIVE_SKIPS` EMPTY, so the guard permits no skip at all — *"the REAL oMLX model list comes back through the relay, from inside the bridge"* PASSED in 2008 ms. **(b) The environment objection is retired on its own terms.** This note predicted the live path *"will not hold on a CI runner or on native Docker"* because it leaned on Lima's host-gateway forwarding reaching macOS loopback. It holds: the same probe passes on `ubuntu-latest` with native Docker, where the container dials the in-bridge alias and a real oMLX answers. What made that possible is transport, not a loosened assertion — `.github/scripts/omlx-shim.ts` binds `0.0.0.0:8000` on the runner and proxies to the operator's server over a Cloudflare tunnel, so the runner's `localhost:8000` behaves as the operator's Mac does and NO line of `src/` changed to accommodate CI. **(c) ISC-257's *"in NO CI job at all"* is simply no longer true.** **The dependency, stated rather than buried:** the SERVER is still one machine, so this job needs the operator's oMLX awake and the tunnel up. That bounds availability, not validity — the criterion is about what a container can reach, and the reaching is now re-checked by a runner rather than attested by a laptop.
- [x] ISC-51: That call succeeds with no route OFF THE BRIDGE SUBNET. **[PARTIAL 2026-08-19 — DOWNGRADED from [x], and the criterion itself RE-WORDED, by the PR #18 security review]** The previous wording was "with no route to the public internet" and it was closed on evidence that had been FALSIFIED: a container on the deny-all bridge, with no relay running, pulls `SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6p1 Ubuntu-3ubuntu13.13` off the bridge gateway `172.18.0.1:22`. Docker's internal-network isolation lives in the FORWARD chain (`! -d 172.18.0.0/16 -i br-<id> -j DROP`), but the gateway is ON-LINK and inside that subnet, so gateway-destined traffic is delivered through INPUT (policy ACCEPT) and is never filtered. The old evidence probed `1.1.1.1` and `example.com` and never measured the gateway — sampling is precisely what missed it. See SRD §12.8's 2026-08-19 erratum for the full measurement and the decision to accept it as a residual. **What is now proved, and how:** `test/integration/relay.test.ts` ENUMERATES rather than samples — exactly one on-link route and zero default routes, read from `/proc/net/route`, which bounds the whole address space instead of five points in it; plus non-zero-exit probes for a public IP, a public name, the LAN oMLX candidate, the Lima host address and the cloud metadata address. The gateway residual is asserted as a POSITIVE (discovered from a non-internal network first, so the assertion is not circular), which converts the finding into a regression test: if the gateway is ever hardened, that test fails and this criterion can be tightened. **Why still `[~]` and not `[x]`:** the reachable set is `{relay ports} ∪ {gateway ports} ∪ {sibling container ports}` and is NOT fixed — anything the host or a sibling binds later joins it with no code change — so the criterion holds as re-worded but the posture is not the closed set the original wording implied. ISC-261 tracks re-taking this against an enumerated reachable set. **[CLOSED 2026-08-23 — the gateway is CONTAINED, and the assertion that recorded the hole was INVERTED rather than deleted.]** The residual this criterion carried since 2026-08-19 is gone. `ensureEgressNetwork` now installs `iptables -I INPUT -i br-<id> -d <gateway> -j DROP` on the Docker host and REFUSES to return a network it could not contain, so "internal" and "actually contained" are one call rather than two. **Why the rule is in INPUT and why that was the whole defect:** Docker implements `--internal` as `! -d <subnet> -i br-<id> -j DROP` in FORWARD, which bounds traffic LEAVING the bridge; the gateway is on-link and inside that subnet, so gateway-destined packets are delivered through INPUT (policy ACCEPT) and are never evaluated by the isolation rule at all. No amount of FORWARD hardening reaches them. **Where the privilege comes from, which is the part that was not obvious:** pifleet is an unprivileged user-space CLI with no CAP_NET_ADMIN, it must not call `sudo`, and on macOS it cannot run `iptables` at all. It does hold the Docker daemon, so the rule is written by a privileged container joined to the host's network and mount namespaces — `docker run --privileged --pid host --network host --entrypoint nsenter <RELAY_IMAGE> -t 1 -m -n -i iptables …` — which borrows the HOST's own iptables binary rather than shipping one. That targets the right netns in every topology: on Linux the daemon's host is the machine, and on macOS/colima it is the Lima VM, which is precisely the host whose listeners a worker could reach. It reuses the already-pinned `RELAY_IMAGE` digest (measured to contain `nsenter` but not `iptables`), so no second image is pulled, pinned or re-pinned; the digest moved to `src/security/pinned-image.ts` to keep `network.ts -> gateway-block.ts` from closing an import cycle back through `relay.ts`. **PROVEN, and proven the hard way — as a mutation, before any of it was written:** on a throwaway `--internal` network a container probing the gateway printed `REACHABLE`; with the rule installed it printed `UNREACHABLE(timeout)`; with the rule removed the network tore down clean. Separately verified that the rule does not break what the fleet needs — container-to-container traffic and Docker's embedded DNS both survive it, because neither is gateway-destined (internal-network DNS answers at 127.0.0.11 inside the worker's own namespace). **The regression test is the SAME LINE that used to assert the hole.** `test/integration/relay.test.ts` enumerated all 65535 ports and asserted `expect(reachable).toContain(hostNsPort)` as a positive; its docstring predicted that a failure there would be good news to be written into the SRD rather than "fixed" by deleting the line. That is exactly what happened, so the assertion is now `expect(reachable).not.toContain(hostNsPort)` plus `expect(reachable).toEqual([])`. **The empty set is asserted as an equality, not as a loop, because a loop over an empty array passes for a scanner that is simply broken** — the vacuous shape this file was rewritten to eliminate. What rules that out is the same scanner, same script, same range, run against an ordinary bridge in the same test: it must still come back with both planted beacons, and its set must still be a strict subset of the kernel socket table. **One thing the fix broke, and what it revealed:** `test/integration/up-wiring.test.ts` drives `up` through a PATH `docker` shim that is deliberately built to fail loudly on any argv it does not recognise — "a silent `exit 0` stand-in would absorb a changed docker invocation instead of surfacing it" — and it did exactly that, turning 27 tests red on the first CI run. The shim was then found to be unfaithful in a second way the containment change exposed: its `network inspect` answered with no `IPAM` at all and a network `Id` of `"wiring-shim"`, which is 11 characters and not hex. Real Docker ids are 64 hex characters and the bridge name is `br-<first 12>` of them, so the id was not a stand-in for a network id — it was a label that had never been read as one. Both were fixed by making the shim MORE faithful rather than by making the product more permissive: real-shaped ids, a real IPAM gateway, and an `iptables` branch that MODELS STATE — `-C` reports absent until `-I` has run and present afterwards, so the insert and the verify-after-insert are not both satisfied by a shim that answers 0 to everything. **What this does NOT close:** ISC-57 stays `[~]`. Sibling containers on the bridge are still reachable and are still "hosts other than the oMLX endpoint", so the loose direction is narrowed from `{gateway ports} ∪ {sibling ports}` to `{sibling ports}` rather than emptied. `down` deliberately does NOT remove the rule, for the same reason it leaves the network and the relay standing: the network outlives the run, and a rule torn down with it would reopen the hole for whatever attaches to that same bridge next. **[GROUNDS REFRESHED 2026-08-26 — the GRADE is unchanged; the reachable-set sentence above went stale when ISC-263's CONNECT proxy landed.]** This entry's set — `{relay ports} u {gateway ports} u {sibling ports}` — was complete while the relay was a port forwarder. It is not any more: `3128` is a door rather than a port, so the set carries a `{3128 -> POLICY}` term that no port scan can measure. Nothing about THIS criterion loosened — the gateway is still contained at layer 3 and the 65535-port scan still comes back empty — but the containment story needed the door measured too, and ISC-263's closing probe does exactly that, including a `DENY_GATEWAY` case proving the proxy will not dial the very gateway this criterion closed.
- [x] ISC-52: A model outside `models_allowlist` is refused at `up` with exit 2.
- [x] ISC-53: A model that answers a `tools`-bearing probe with prose is refused at `up` with exit 2. **[CLOSED 2026-08-19, Group E]** `security/model-probe.ts` sends one `tools`-bearing completion per DISTINCT resolved model (deduped — six workers on one model is the normal §5.9 F40 shape, and six real generations to learn one fact is a tax on every `up`), and refuses unless BOTH `finish_reason === "tool_calls"` and a non-empty `tool_calls[]` come back; either half alone lets through a server claiming a call it did not make. The refusal is a `ConfigError` subclass, so exit 2 is inherited from the machinery ISC-52 already uses rather than restated. Proven at the CLI, not just at the module: `test/integration/up-wiring.test.ts` → `the native-tool-call probe gates the launch path (ISC-53)` runs the real `up` against a stub oMLX that answers in prose and asserts exit 2, a message naming `eng-1`/`wiring-test-model`/`require_native_tool_calls`, and — the part that makes "launches nothing" a fact rather than a claim — an empty `workersDir` and an empty ledger. Mutation-proved: replacing `await assertModelsSupportToolCalls(...)` in `up.ts` with a no-op turns 4 of that describe's 5 tests red (re-measured 2026-08-19 after the review fixes; it was 3 of 4 before `the gate is ON by default` was added), so the wiring is held in place by tests rather than by hope. The comparison runs ONLY against a model list actually fetched (`allowlistChecked`). An unreachable endpoint serves nothing, so an ungated check would report every entry missing and send an operator to edit a correct allowlist — and on the DEFAULT config that would fire on every developer machine on every run, since `llm.base_url` names `host.docker.internal`, which does not resolve from the host `doctor` probes from. That is the same trap this file's own vantage note records as having "turned eight green runs red", so the guard is asserted rather than merely intended. Both files run under CI's plain `bun test test/unit` / `bun test test/integration`, with no Docker gate, no `skipIf`, and no oMLX. (3) LIVE, local only — against the real oMLX on this host, which serves `Qwen3-Embedding-4B-4bit-DWQ`, `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-4bit` and `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-4bit`: `fleet.example.yaml`'s three names give `omlx allowlist: 0/3 served` and exit 3, reproducing the motivating finding above exactly — including that `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-8bit` misses the served `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-4bit` by a single character. Its only consumers are `test/unit/render.test.ts` and `test/e2e/scale-16-workers.test.ts`. Both ISC-61 tests exercise library functions rather than the launch path: `test/unit/render.test.ts:1011` calls `renderAllWorkers` directly, and `test/unit/config.test.ts:501` calls `resolveAllWorkers`, whose sole production caller (`doctor.ts:747`) uses it to collect the distinct TOOLCHAIN set for image checks and never consumes its length. **What production actually does.** `up.ts` derives its launch set from argv alone — `.option("--workers <ids>", ..., "eng-1")` at `up.ts:112`, split and de-duplicated at `up.ts:182`. The single occurrence of `config.workers` in `up.ts` (line 88, `assertModelsAllowed`) is a MEMBERSHIP set for the model allowlist and is explicitly written to `continue` past any id the config does not define. Every other `config.workers` reader in `src/` is likewise membership or reporting: `load.ts:276/279` (lookup), `model-probe.ts:541`, `materialize.ts:533` (membership), `config.ts:29` (`config validate` prints the ids). `up.ts:105`'s own comment concedes it — "the worker list comes from `--workers` until then". **Measured rather than inferred**, real CLI, headless backend, fake-pi double, no config file present: `up --backend headless --json` with no `--workers` flag launched exactly one worker, `eng-1`, the commander default string; `up --backend headless --workers a1,b2,c3 --json` launched three workers named `a1`, `b2`, `c3` — three ids no config defines. The count follows argv unconditionally, so editing `workers:` "with no other edit" changes nothing. **`[ ]` and not `[~]`:** there is no weaker true statement about the launch path to preserve, because the launch path never reads the list. **Wiring that would close it:** have `up` default its worker set to `loaded.config.workers` when `--workers` is absent (make the commander default `undefined` rather than `"eng-1"`), and render through `renderAllWorkers` instead of per-id `renderWorker`; then re-take the evidence at the CLI — two configs differing only in `workers:` length, asserting the `up --json` worker array length tracks it — rather than at the module. **[UNBLOCKED 2026-08-20 by the container launcher (ISC-286/287): the runtime path this criterion was waiting on now exists — `up` records a launch argv and the supervisor spawns it, so a container can be inspected, exec'd into and torn down. The note is here so the next reader does not re-derive that the blocker was absence of a launcher.]** **[CLOSED 2026-08-20, Phase F of SRD-PIFLEET-002.]** `--workers`' commander default `"eng-1"` is removed (`up.ts:146`), the launch set defaults to `loaded.config.workers` (`up.ts:441`), and `renderAllWorkers` gained an optional id list — giving it its first real `src/` caller and closing the RC-1 unreachable-module finding. Evidence is taken AT THE CLI on `up --json`'s worker array, never at the module. **The measurement that matters most, and the reason this entry existed:** under the mutation that restores the `"eng-1"` default, the two PRE-EXISTING module-level ISC-61 tests (`render.test.ts`, `config.test.ts`) both STAY GREEN — `2 pass, 0 fail` — while production launches one worker for a three-worker config. That is this criterion's original defect reproduced on demand: module-level tests cannot see a launch path that never calls the module, which is exactly how it was graded `[x]` while being false. No further module-level tests were added, deliberately. Ids named by `--workers` that the config does not define are still accepted, unchanged; only the DEFAULT moved, and on the default path every id comes from `workers:`, so the membership skips in `assertModelsAllowed` and the image gate become unreachable rather than wider. No config and no `--workers` is now `EXIT.USAGE` rather than an invented `eng-1`.

- [x] ISC-69: `up` returns a `run_id`.

- [x] ISC-74: Anti: no `FleetBackend` implementation launches or signals a supervisor; the lifecycle is `SupervisorLauncher`'s, which no backend implements. **[RESTATED AND CLOSED 2026-08-25, per owner decision, on the ISC-157/192/246 precedent for a criterion whose literal wording cannot be tested on this platform. The ORIGINAL sentence — *"Closing a worker's pane does not stop the worker in rpc mode; the task still settles"* — and the full record of the probe that was written and deleted are preserved verbatim below, because the measurement is what justifies the restatement.]** **WHY RESTATED RATHER THAN BUILT.** The deleted probe's finding stands: `tmux kill-session` terminates only the pane's IMMEDIATE process on this platform, so a `Bun.spawn` child is orphaned and survives whether or not it was detached. The criterion is very probably TRUE and `detached: true` is not what makes it true in the pane-close case. Any probe of the original wording therefore asserts a property that holds unconditionally — a guard nobody has seen fail, which this repo's standing rule refuses. **WHAT THE RESTATEMENT GRADES, and the trade stated plainly:** the MECHANISM (nothing in the view layer can reach a supervisor's lifecycle), not the OUTCOME (a closed pane leaves the task settling). ISC-77/78 already own the process-tree facts the outcome rests on. **IT IS TRUE BY DESIGN AND NOW BY TEST.** `src/backends/types.ts` says so in its own header — `SupervisorLauncher` is a SEPARATE, backend-independent interface precisely because an earlier design made the supervisor a pane child and contradicted SRD §3.3 — and `test/unit/anti-criteria.test.ts` turns that comment into something that can fail. **TWO PROBES, because one is satisfiable by an empty tree.** (1) No file under `src/backends/**` outside `types.ts` names any lifecycle machinery — `launchDetached`, `processLauncher`, `supervisorArgv`, `SupervisorLauncher`, `runKillLadder`, `killWedged`, `process.kill`, `SIGKILL`, `SIGTERM`, `safety/kill`, `safety/reaper`, `supervisor/launch` — read with comments STRIPPED, since backends legitimately discuss the boundary and banning the noun `supervisor` would fail on the three files that document it most carefully. `types.ts` is excluded as DECLARATION: it is where the separation under test is defined. (2) The `FleetBackend` interface declares no method naming launch, kill, signal or spawn — without which a future `launchWorker` would pass the source scan in every existing file while making the criterion false for every backend written after it. **MUTATION-PROVED, both restored byte-identical:** a `runKillLadder` reference added to `backends/headless/index.ts` reddens the first; a `launchWorker` method added to `FleetBackend` reddens the second. **THE `rpc mode` QUALIFIER IS GONE with the original wording, and nothing in the restatement distinguishes rpc from any other mode — which is honest, since nothing in the deleted attempt did either.** **[ORIGINAL ENTRY PRESERVED:]** Closing a worker's pane does not stop the worker in rpc mode; the task still settles. **STAYS OPEN — a test was written for this and then DELETED, because a mutation proved it could not fail. [AUDITED 2026-08-19 by the referenced-criteria grading audit.]** **The existing reference is not evidence.** `grep -rn ISC-74 test/` returns one hit, `test/unit/voided.test.ts:72`, which asserts the id is ABSENT from the attended-mode voided table. That is a statement about a documentation table, not about panes; it would pass unchanged if closing a pane killed every worker in the fleet. **The adjacent coverage is real but is a proxy.** `test/integration/supervisor.test.ts` proves the process-tree facts the guarantee is built on — `pgid == pid`, no controlling tty (ISC-77/78), survives a dead launcher and reparents to PID 1 (ISC-75/76) — but never closes a pane, and a process-tree shape is the mechanism, not the outcome the criterion states. **What was attempted:** a `test/integration/pane-close.test.ts` driving a real tmux server on a private `-L` socket, launching the supervisor from INSIDE the pane (the stricter v1.1 arrangement `launch.ts`'s header names, chosen deliberately because production's arrangement — pane runs only the log viewer, supervisor launched separately — makes the assertion vacuous), dispatching a `slow-turn.json` task, killing the session mid-turn, then asserting the supervisor's (pid, start-time) identity is unchanged, that `T-PANE-1` settles `success`, and that the control socket still answers. It passed in 6s. **It was deleted because the mutation did not fail it.** Removing `detached: true` from `processLauncher.launchDetached` left it GREEN. Probed directly to find out why: a `Bun.spawn` child of a pane command shares the pane's pgid and tty (`ps` shows both at pgid 98379, `S+`, `ttys003`), but `tmux kill-session` terminates only the pane's IMMEDIATE process — the child was orphaned, dropped to `S`, and SURVIVED. tmux does not signal the pane's whole process group here, so on this platform a supervisor cannot be stopped by pane closure whether or not it is detached, and the test asserted a property that holds unconditionally. Per this repo's standing rule — a guard nobody has seen fail is indistinguishable from one that cannot fail — shipping it would have added 6s of CI time and a false checkbox, so it was removed rather than kept as decoration. **What this measurement means for the criterion:** it is very probably TRUE, and `detached: true` is not what makes it true in the pane-close case; ISC-77/78 already own the properties detachment actually delivers. Closing it honestly needs either a falsifiable observable (a backend arrangement in which pane teardown CAN reach the worker — e.g. a container-per-pane backend, or `respawn-pane`/`kill-server` paths that signal differently) or an acceptance that the criterion is structural, in which case it should be re-worded as an anti-criterion in the ISC-137 shape — "no `FleetBackend` method launches or signals a supervisor" — which IS mechanically checkable against `src/`. The `rpc mode` qualifier is also unexercised: nothing in the attempt distinguished rpc from any other mode.
